5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 3

Past simple: irregular verbs

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Recognise irregular verbs (verbos irregulares) in a text
  • Learn the 30 most common irregular past forms
  • Use irregular verbs in affirmative, negative and question sentences
  • Tell a short story in the past

Para pensar

Si «jugué» es played, ¿por qué «fui» no es goed?

Explicación

What is an irregular verb?

Regular verbs add -ed: play → played. Irregular verbs don't follow this rule. Each one has its own past form: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, have → had.

The good news: like regular verbs, the past form is the same for all persons: «I went», «she went», «they went». And irregular verbs are very common, so you hear them all the time in songs, films and stories. En castellano: nosotros también tenemos irregulares: «ir» → «fui», no «í». En inglés es igual: hay que memorizarlos.

The top ten

Start with the ten most useful irregular verbs. You will use them every day: go → went (ir), have → had (tener), get → got (conseguir, llegar), make → made (hacer, fabricar), do → did (hacer), see → saw (ver), come → came (venir), eat → ate (comer), take → took (coger, llevar), say → said (decir).

«I went to the park and I saw my friends. We had a picnic and we ate sandwiches. Then Marc came with his dog and said hello.»

Learn them in families

Many irregular verbs change in a similar way. Learn them in families. i → a: swim → swam, sing → sang, drink → drank, begin → began, ring → rang. -ought / -aught: buy → bought, bring → brought, think → thought, catch → caught, teach → taught.

ee → e / ea → e: sleep → slept, feel → felt, meet → met, keep → kept. o-e: write → wrote, ride → rode, drive → drove. Same form: put → put, cut → cut, hit → hit, let → let. Consejo: agrupados se recuerdan mucho mejor que en una lista por orden alfabético.

More useful verbs

Here are more irregular verbs for your stories: run → ran, sit → sat, stand → stood, fall → fell, find → found, lose → lost, win → won, give → gave, tell → told, read → read (it is written the same but sounds «red»), wear → wore, fly → flew, know → knew, leave → left, break → broke.

«The bird flew away.» «Our team won the match!» «I lost my keys, but my brother found them under the sofa.» «Grandpa told us a story.»

Negatives: didn't + base form

The negative works exactly like with regular verbs: didn't + the base form (the verb as in the dictionary). «I didn't go to the party.» «She didn't eat her vegetables.» «We didn't see the eclipse.»

This is a big help: in negatives you don't need the irregular form. Not «I didn't went», not «She didn't ate». En castellano: piensa que did ya «lleva» el pasado; el verbo vuelve a ser el de siempre. Solo tienes que acordarte del irregular en las frases afirmativas.

Questions: Did…? Where did…?

Questions also use did + subject + base form: «Did you see the fireworks?» «Yes, I did.» «Did he take the bus?» «No, he didn't. He walked.»

With question words: «Where did you go on holiday?» «What did you eat?» «Who did you meet?» «What time did the train leave?» The answer uses the irregular past: «I went to Galicia.» «I ate octopus.» «I met my cousins.»

Tricks to remember them

1. Flashcards: write the verb on one side and the past on the other. Practise five every day. 2. Rhythm: say them with a beat, clapping: «go – went, see – saw, eat – ate!». 3. Memory game: place the cards face down and find the pairs.

4. Your own sentences: use each new verb in a true sentence about you: «Last summer I swam in the sea.» 5. Read stories: stories in the past are full of irregular verbs. Consejo: no intentes aprender cien de golpe. Con los treinta de este tema ya puedes contar casi cualquier cosa.

Reading: the lost dog

Read this story: «Last Sunday, Max woke up early and took his dog Coco to the park. Coco saw a squirrel and ran after it. Max called her, but she didn't come back. Max felt very worried. He looked everywhere and asked people. An old lady said: "I saw a small dog near the fountain." Max went there and he found Coco. She was wet and happy! They had an ice cream and came home.»

Underline the irregular verbs in red and the regular ones in blue. What did Coco see? Where did Max find her?

Let's practise: chain story

Play a chain story in groups of four. The first person says a sentence with an irregular verb: «Yesterday a dragon came to our school.» The next person continues: «It ate all the sandwiches.» «Then it flew to the gym.» «Finally it fell asleep in the library!»

Write your story and draw it in four pictures. Check each verb: is it regular or irregular? Did you use the base form after didn't? Repaso: afirmativa con la forma irregular; negativa y pregunta con did + verbo básico.

Irregular verbs

Ejercicios

  1. Write the past: go, have, see, make.

  2. Write the past: sing, drink, think, catch.

  3. Complete: «Yesterday I ___ (eat) paella.»

  4. Complete: «My aunt ___ (give) me a book.»

  5. Make it negative: «We took a taxi.»

  6. Make a question: «She wrote a poem.»

  7. Ask with what: «He bought a skateboard.»

  8. Correct: «I didn't saw the match, but my team winned.»

  9. Which family? «keep → kept»

  10. Write four sentences about your best day with irregular verbs.

Practica

  1. The past of «go» is…

    1. A) goed
    2. B) gone
    3. C) went

  2. The past of «eat» is…

    1. A) ate
    2. B) eated
    3. C) eat

  3. The past of «buy» is…

    1. A) buyed
    2. B) bought
    3. C) brought

  4. The past of «swim» is…

    1. A) swimmed
    2. B) swam
    3. C) swum

  5. «I didn't ___ the film.»

    1. A) saw
    2. B) seen
    3. C) see

  6. «Did you ___ a good time?»

    1. A) have
    2. B) had
    3. C) has

  7. The past of «put» is…

    1. A) putted
    2. B) pat
    3. C) put

  8. «Where did they go?» — «They ___ to Paris.»

    1. A) go
    2. B) went
    3. C) did go

  9. The past of «sleep» is…

    1. A) slept
    2. B) sleeped
    3. C) slep

  10. Which verb is irregular?

    1. A) write
    2. B) walk
    3. C) play

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué diferencia hay entre un verbo regular y uno irregular; Cuáles son los diez irregulares más usados y su pasado; Por qué en negativas y preguntas no se usa la forma irregular; Qué trucos ayudan a memorizarlos.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

go → wentir → fui.
have → hadtener → tuve.
see → sawver → vi.
eat → atecomer → comí.
buy → boughtcomprar (familia -ought).
swim → swamnadar (familia i → a).
put → putIgual en presente y pasado.
didn't + base formI didn't go (no «didn't went»).

Soluciones

  1. C) Irregular.
  2. A) Irregular.
  3. B) Familia -ought.
  4. B) i → a.
  5. C) Tras didn't, forma básica.
  6. A) Tras did, forma básica.
  7. C) Igual que el presente.
  8. B) Respuesta en afirmativa: went.
  9. A) ee → e.
  10. A) write → wrote.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. went, had, saw, made.
  2. sang, drank, thought, caught.
  3. ate.
  4. gave.
  5. We didn't take a taxi.
  6. Did she write a poem?
  7. What did he buy?
  8. I didn't see the match, but my team won.
  9. ee → e, como sleep → slept y feel → felt.
  10. Model answer: I went to the beach. I swam in the sea. We had lunch in a restaurant. I felt very happy.
